figurative_meaning_en: Failing at the very end of a task or effort
similar_in_english: Snatching defeat from the jaws of victory
example_sentences_in_bangla: সে প্রজেক্টটি প্রায় শেষ করেই ছিল, কিন্তু তীরে এসে তরী ডোবা, শেষ মুহূর্তে একটা ভুলে সব নষ্ট হয়ে গেল।
খেলায় তারা জিততে চলেছিল, কিন্তু তীরে এসে তরী ডোবা, শেষ গোলে আত্মগোল করে ফেলল।
example_sentences_in_english: He was almost done with the project, but like a boat sinking at the shore, a last-minute mistake ruined everything.
They were about to win the game, but snatching defeat from the jaws of victory, they scored an own goal at the end.
history: This idiom originates from the riverine culture of Bengal, where boats (tori) were common for transport, symbolizing the frustration of a safe journey ending in disaster just before reaching the shore.
note: Reflects the precarious nature of life in flood-prone, river-dependent regions of Bengal.
